subject: Renewal trigger, opt-out process, and termination-for-convenience fee — Acme Corp MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme MSA — redline ask: termination/renewal mechanics

Laura / Marissa,

Acme (procurement + legal copied below) pushed a redline set that changes term/renewal mechanics in a few ways. I attached their marked-up MSA and the draft order form they want to use — key asks summarized below: 

- Auto-renew cadence: 12 months (we're currently proposing 12; they want explicit auto-renew unless they opt out)
- Notice window: they want a 45-day opt-out window prior to renewal
- Termination for convenience: they want the right anytime with pro-rated refund; no exit fee for first 12 months
- Early termination / refund mechanics: they propose refund of unused prepaid and a 30-day concurrency for subscriptions starting mid-term

Acme says their procurement cycle requires the flexibility to align budgets across business units; their legal flagged the 90-day convenience fee and 60-day notice in our standard. They asked if we can soften fees or shorten notice to 45 days, and if we can commit contractually to an easy opt-out flow (order form checkbox + email notice).

Questions for legal: 
1) Is 45 days acceptable vs. our standard 60? Any operational concerns about implementation in the console (billing cutoff dates)?
2) Refund / fee compromise we could accept to protect forecasted revenue (examples: 60-day fee equals 1x monthly invoice in year 1, no fee after year 1; or pro-rated refund but minimum 30 days fee).
3) Anything in the redlines that creates compliance or SLA exposure (e.g., obligation to provide data exports on termination within narrow windows)?

My recommendation is to offer a middle ground: 45-day opt-out, termination-for-convenience allowed with a 60-day fee in year 1 (capped at one monthly invoice), and pro-rated refunds after that. If we need to waive fees entirely, we should require VP approval. 

I'm looping legal to confirm. If approved, I'll send a tracked redline back to Acme and propose the order form language for the opt-out checkbox and billing cutoff semantics.

Attachments: Acme_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx; OrderForm_ACME_v3.pdf

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procure@acme.com>, Acme Legal <contracts@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme MSA — redline ask: termination/renewal mechanics

Karthik,

Thanks for the quick note and for summarizing. A few clarifications from our side: 

- 45 days is our preference because our finance team needs time to route renewals across multiple business units. 60 days causes internal calendar conflicts for many of our teams.
- On termination-for-convenience, we do not expect an immediate full refund; our goal is to avoid being locked in for another year if product fit shifts. Requested language: pro-rated refund of unused prepaid with no termination fee within first 12 months. After 12 months, standard notice applies.
- For operational implementation, we'd prefer the opt-out to be an explicit checkbox in the order form and an email notice to a contract inbox (procure@acme.com) — we can provide a sample text.

We attached a marked-up order form to show the checkbox placement. If Redwood needs to preserve some revenue protection, we'd accept a short transition / wind-down window (e.g., 30 days of service transition) but would like that to be handled as a credit rather than an upfront fee.

Happy to jump on a call if that helps move faster. Our procurement lead (cc'd) is available Thursday afternoon PT.

Best,
Jane Doe
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp

Date: 2026-07-01T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme MSA — redline ask: termination/renewal mechanics

Thanks for the summary, Karthik — and thanks Jane for the context. Below is a proposed position that balances Acme's request for flexibility with Redwood's revenue protection and operational constraints. Please treat as internal draft until we confirm with Finance/Revenue Ops.

Proposed compromise: 
- Renewal trigger / opt-out: Auto-renew every 12 months with an opt-out notice window of 45 days prior to renewal. We will accept 45 days (instead of our standard 60) in this deal given the enterprise nature and likelihood of expansion. Operational note: Revenue Ops will need to set billing cutoff to align with the 45-day date and ensure the Console reflects the opt-out status.

- Termination for convenience: Allow termination at any time with a pro-rated refund of prepaid amounts for unused full months. In year 1 (first 12 months after initial effective date), we will apply a short transition charge equal to one monthly invoice as liquidated damages to cover provisioning/onboarding costs. After 12 months, no liquidated damages; pro-rated refund only. 

- Implementation detail: The opt-out will be an explicit checkbox in the order form and require notice to procure@acme.com. Redwood will provide the sample notice text; acceptance triggers the opt-out on the renewal in our system.

- Approval gating: Any deviation that eliminates the year-1 transition charge entirely must be escalated for VP/CRO approval. Discounts or full fee waivers should be tied to a compensating commercial concession (e.g., committed minimums or earlier payment terms).

Operational asks from Sales (Karthik / Marissa): 
1) Confirm whether Acme will accept the 1x monthly transition charge in year 1 as the compromise (Jane, does that work?)
2) If yes, we will prepare an updated MSA redline and an order form mock with the opt-out checkbox. I will include precise language for the refund calculation and billing cutoff dates.
3) Revenue Ops: please weigh in on billing cutoffs and the Console opt-out flag (added to the related_links folder).

Jane — if you can confirm on the 1x monthly transition charge, we can send a tracked redline today and request signature via DocuSign.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
